schedules.title: Memory curation
schedules.description: Keeps your second brain tidy: files durable learnings from recent chats, applies accepted memory proposals, and updates project notes when something changed. Reports only what it processed; does nothing on a quiet day.
schedules.prompt: Curate recent archived chats, memory proposals, and durable learnings. Use the memory agent. Prefer existing session-insights sections and update the configured vault; append durable learnings to `Workspace/Learnings.md`. Do not edit the bounded `ciao:memory` or `ciao:profile` regions: one `CLAUDE.md` is shared by every workspace, so a per-workspace run promoting into it would leak that workspace's facts into all the others. Leave cross-project facts in the proposals queue for the user to promote; project facts belong in the project's canonical doc. File people in this workspace's `People/`; a contact you deal with here belongs here, even if you first met them in another workspace's chat. Use `memory_status` to inspect usage. Report malformed expiration tags instead of guessing. File a fact into its destination first, then dismiss that proposal with `memory_proposal_resolve` (the reverse can lose it). Leave proposals that belong in a bounded region queued. If nothing new needs processing, reply with a one-line no-op and stop. Then report: processed counts, changed files, and — listed in full, one numbered line each — every cross-project fact you left queued for a bounded region, so the user can reply naming which to promote.

schedules.title: Install health
schedules.description: Weekly check of the parts of this install that are shared by every workspace: unresolved background job failures and pending upgrade actions. Reported once rather than once per workspace, because the findings are the same in each.
schedules.prompt: Run `ciao os-audit --json --scope global`. That scope covers only what every workspace shares: unresolved background job failures and pending upgrade actions. Exit code 1 means it found items needing attention; continue. Exit code 2 means it could not inspect required evidence reliably; report its scan errors and do not claim the install is healthy. Summarize command output instead of pasting raw JSON. Fix nothing: an upgrade action is optional and a job failure needs its own diagnosis. Report the failing jobs with their errors, the pending upgrade actions with what each suggests, and any scan errors. If the audit is reliable and clean, reply with a one-line no-op and stop.

schedules.title: Workspace hygiene
schedules.description: Weekly AI OS health check for this workspace: audits knowledge, skills, instructions, bounded memory, and unresolved automation failures, and repairs safe link drift.
schedules.prompt: Run a hygiene pass for THIS workspace only. Summarize command output instead of pasting raw JSON. Steps: 1) Run `ciao vault-index --write` to regenerate this root's INDEX.md and VOCABULARY.md from note frontmatter. The `--write` flag is required. The audit below reads what this writes, so it must run first; if it fails, report the failure plainly and do not claim the workspace is healthy. 2) Run `ciao os-audit --json --scope workspace`. It scopes its evidence to the active workspace automatically; do not pass another workspace's name. The `workspace` scope omits background job failures and upgrade actions on purpose: those are the same for every workspace and the install-health routine reports them once. Exit code 1 means the audit ran and found items needing attention; continue. Exit code 2 means it could not inspect required evidence reliably; report its scan errors and do not claim the workspace is healthy. 3) When the audit is reliable, apply only low-risk, unambiguous fixes in this workspace's vault: repair or remove dead links, fix obvious MEMORY.md drift where entries point at files that moved or no longer exist, and rename a non-canonical `type:` whose target VOCABULARY.md already names. Do not rewrite instruction conflicts, skills, orphaned notes, duplicates, invalid expiration tags, or schedule prompts. 4) Re-run `ciao os-audit --json --scope workspace` to verify what remains. 5) Report initial and final issue counts, what was fixed, unresolved findings, and scan errors. If the first reliable audit is healthy and the index rebuild changed nothing, reply with a one-line no-op and stop.

schedules.title: Skill evolution
schedules.description: Weekly look at how your custom skills performed: reviews recent sessions for errors and corrections and drafts improvement proposals for skills that struggled. Proposals are saved for your review — nothing is applied automatically, and it does nothing if you have no custom skills.
schedules.prompt: Run `python3 -m ciao.skill_evolution` with the workspace default model. Summarize proposals written and any failed gates. Do not apply proposals automatically, and do not edit native memory unless the curation workflow explicitly calls for it.
